subject.title: feat(gateway): pre-handshake WS verifyClient with Sec-Fetch-Site and forwarded-header hardening

question: Should pre-handshake WebSocket hardening be integrated into the existing Gateway origin/trusted-proxy policy, or should OpenClaw introduce a separate `gateway.security` configuration boundary with a default-on `Sec-Fetch-Site` rejection?
rationale: The choice determines a public security/configuration contract and whether existing explicitly permitted browser flows may be rejected before the current admission policy runs; code review cannot choose that compatibility boundary safely.

options.title: Integrate existing policy
options.body: Reuse the established Control UI origin and trusted-proxy settings, keep current accepted flows compatible by default, and add only checks that preserve policy parity.

options.title: Adopt separate strict policy
options.body: Keep `gateway.security`, but document and prove its interaction with every existing origin setting and require an explicit upgrade decision for any default-on rejection.

options.title: Narrow to header consistency
options.body: Land only forwarded-header validation after fixing IPv6 parsing, and defer fetch-metadata and new configuration direction to a coordinated Gateway security change.

recommendation.title: Integrate existing policy
recommendation.body: Reuse the established Control UI origin and trusted-proxy settings, keep current accepted flows compatible by default, and add only checks that preserve policy parity.

likelyOwner.reason: The supplied discussion identifies this person with the Gateway origin/security boundary, and current-main history shows extensive ownership of the affected paths.
